samples.summary: New undo/redo clear test uses optional chaining with `toBeUndefined()`, so the clear and redo assertions pass vacuously if the block or inline disappears
samples.evidence: `expect(store.getBlock(block.id)?.inlines[0].style.bold).toBeUndefined()` (after the clear, and again after `redo()`) is satisfied whenever `getBlock` returns undefined — i.e. if `removeStyleByPath` / redo corrupted or dropped the block entirely the test still goes green. The neighbouring 'applyStyle → undo → style removed' test guards against exactly this by asserting `text` is still 'Hello'; the new test asserts no text/structure invariant at all. Only the two `toBe(true)` assertions are non-vacuous.

samples.summary: No test covers a mixed write where styleByPath merge and removeStyleByPath both fire (set one key while clearing another)
samples.evidence: `applyStyle` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1884-1892) re-merges `{...existingAttrs, ...styleAttrs}` and *then* removes `removeAttrs`. The order matters: a write like `{ bold: true, italic: undefined }` re-writes the stale `italic` from existingAttrs before removing it. The new test only exercises the pure-clear case `{ bold: undefined }`, and no other test in the file passes both a defined and an undefined key in one call, so a regression in the merge/remove ordering or in surviving sibling attributes would not be caught.

samples.summary: `expect('bold' in (cd?.style ?? {})).toBe(false)` passes vacuously when the run lookup fails
samples.evidence: `cd` is found by `inlines.find((i) => i.text === 'cd')`; the `?? {}` fallback makes the new bold assertion true whenever `cd` is undefined (e.g. if normalizeInlines merged runs differently). The italic assertion above it (`toBe(false)`) does fail in that case, so the test is not wholly vacuous, but the assertion added by this delta is not independently load-bearing. Asserting `expect(cd).toBeDefined()` (or dropping the `?? {}`) would make the mixed-branch claim in the new comment real.

samples.summary: Merging the two writes into one dropped the only coverage of a toggle-off applied to a run that already carries an explicit `false`
samples.evidence: The previous version issued a second `applyInlineStyle(..., { bold: false })` against the run that already had `italic: false` stored; the delta collapses both keys into a single write. Nothing now exercises `styleOffAsClear` on a run whose style already contains an explicit `false` (the re-toggle-off path), where `defaults[key]` is still consulted per block.

finding.summary: The mixed-key branch of `styleOffAsClear` (one style object containing both a style-supplied key and a non-supplied key) is never exercised, though the test comment claims it is
finding.evidence: In 'keeps an explicit false where the named style supplies the flag' (document.test.ts:345-367) the comment at line 360 says "A key the style does not supply is still cleared **in the same write**", but the test issues two *separate* `applyInlineStyle` calls: `{ italic: false }` then `{ bold: false }`. The interesting branch in `styleOffAsClear` (document.ts:405-417) is the copy-on-write path `cleared = cleared ?? { ...style }` combined with `if (defaults[key]) continue`, i.e. a single patch like `{ italic: false, bold: false }` on a Heading 6 where `italic:false` must survive while `bold` is deleted. A regression that built `cleared` as `{}` instead of a spread of `style`, or that cleared/kept the wrong key when both are present, would drop the italic override and no test in the diff or elsewhere would fail. I grepped packages/docs/test for combined boolean-off patches and found none.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test exercises the mixed-key branch of `styleOffAsClear` (one patch containing both a style-supplied key and a non-supplied key), and that the test at document.test.ts:345-364 issues two separate applyInlineStyle calls. Reading the file directly refutes both claims. packages/docs/test/model/document.test.ts:356-359 makes a SINGLE `applyInlineStyle` call with the combined patch `{ italic: false, bold: false }` on a block set to Heading 6 (line 351). Heading 6's built-in inline style is `italic: true` (packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:91), so italic is style-supplied and bold is not — exactly the mixed case. The assertions at lines 362-363 check both halves: `cd?.style.italic` must be `false` (the surviving override) and `'bold' in style` must be `false` (the deleted key). This is a real, non-vacuous discriminator for the branch at document.ts:405-417: if `cleared` were built as `{}` instead of `{ ...style }`, the italic override would be dropped and line 362 would fail; if the `if (defaults[key]) continue` check were inverted, either line 362 or line 363 would fail. The reviewer's quoted evidence about two separate calls does not match the working tree.
